category: Enterprise Architecture, System Hardening & Advanced Threats

content.tldr: Advanced Persistent Threats (APTs) are well-funded, prolonged adversary campaigns targeting high-value assets, requiring layered defense-in-depth controls across every stage of the cyber kill chain.
content.simple_explanation: APTs (often nation-state actors or organized syndicates) do not execute opportunistic spray-and-pray attacks; they target specific organizations over months or years. Their lifecycle follows the Cyber Kill Chain: reconnaissance, targeted weaponization (spear phishing, zero-days), establishing persistence, internal credential harvesting, stealth lateral movement, and data exfiltration. Countering APTs requires Defense-in-Depth: layered security where if perimeter firewalls fail, EDR, network segmentation, multi-factor authentication, and canary tokens detect the intruder.
content.real_world_example: A medieval fortress: surrounding the treasure vault with a deep moat, an outer curtain wall, an inner portcullis, armed patrol guards, and tripwires; breaching the moat does not grant access to the vault.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Single-point defenses inevitably fail against determined adversaries. Defense-in-depth assumes breach, focusing on minimizing dwell time through behavioral analytics and automated containment.
